title: Knowledge Management Officer (KMO) (I) (Maj to Capt) FMOS, DIR C4
raw_text:
23.     MOS 8055, Knowledge Management Officer (KMO) (I) (Maj to Capt) FMOS, DIR
C4

    a. Summary. Information Management Officers enable efficient
information assimilation, sharing, and collaboration to facilitate the
commander's decision-making ability, staff synchronization, and cross
functional area coordination. To determine information management
requirements, Information Management Officers need to conduct a detailed
analysis of the information exchange requirements of the commander, supported
staff functions and processes, and attached units. To determine the
technical requirements and associated C2 support structure, Information
Management Officers must be familiar with characteristics of command-and-
control systems including hardware, software, configuration, and
cybersecurity requirements necessary for employment and fuse their knowledge
of technical system with information exchange requirements. Information
Management Officers work with the commander and staff functional areas to
identify, integrate, and devise solutions to gaps and seams within and across
staff processes. Information Management Officers will also be able to
leverage process improvement techniques as well as technology to develop
innovative and effective solutions to mission requirements. Information
Management Officers identify, leverage, and design collaborative
capabilities, competencies, services, and tools that best support the
commander and staff section during the decision-making process. They
interact with subordinate commanders and Staff Officers throughout the
command and across the war fighting functions (intelligence, fires, maneuver,
logistics, C2, and force protection). This MOS will be assigned as a FMOS
only and is assigned to any unrestricted officer.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Serve in an 8055 billet for 6 months.

        (2) Complete the Information Management Officer Qualification Course
(IMOQ) available through MarineNet (IMOQTRN001).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Command and Control Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Command and Control Center Officers 55-1015.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

Conduct needs assessments to identify document management requirements of departments or end users.

To determine information management requirements, Information Management Officers need to conduct a detailed analysis of the information exchange requirements of the commander, supported staff functions and processes, and attached units.
Identify operational requirements for new systems to inform selection of technological solutions.

Recommend new systems and processes to improve operations.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
